evals.prompt: I'm building the wire/transport layer for a real-time multiplayer shooter on top of UDP. I need to send both per-frame player input and occasional full world snapshots plus the connection handshake. How should I structure the transport API and choose delivery reliability? Describe the send API and how a connection between two participants is set up.
assertions: States that the delivery guarantee (unreliable vs ordered vs reliable/deliver-all) is a property of the packet type, not chosen per individual send call, and reserves reliable delivery for must-arrive data (snapshot/handshake) while player input is sent unreliably
Warns that using reliable-ordered delivery for everything recreates TCP-style head-of-line blocking over UDP (one dropped packet stalls everything queued behind it)
States that a pipe/connection is unidirectional (one-way A to B) so a separate pipe is needed for the return direction

evals.prompt: In my authoritative-server game the server sends per-frame state changes to connected clients. A new client just connected mid-match and its world is garbage/corrupted, while clients that were already connected are fine. What is wrong with my replication approach and how should a newly connected client be handled?
assertions: Identifies that a delta is meaningless without a baseline and that applying deltas to a client that never received the initial full state corrupts its world
States that a freshly connected node must first be sent a full snapshot (complete state dump) to establish its baseline before any incremental delta is applied

evals.prompt: I set up state replication in my engine: my Transform component is marked replicable and I confirmed the same component type replicates fine on other objects. But one specific spawned object's transform never appears on the clients even though nothing errors. What is the most likely cause?
assertions: Identifies that replication requires two independent opt-ins: a per-component replication capability AND a per-object replication flag on the instance
Concludes the specific object instance is not flagged/marked for replication, so nothing about it is sent even though its component type is replicable

evals.prompt: For faster iteration I run my server node and client node inside the same process/executable and step them together in one debugger, routing everything through my network API. It works perfectly locally, but I'm worried about what this setup might hide before we ship to real machines. What should I watch out for and what testing should I add?
assertions: States that in-process/local delivery never drops or reorders packets, so packet-loss and out-of-order bugs stay hidden until tested on a real socket or under injected adverse conditions
Recommends injecting simulated adverse network conditions (artificial latency and/or bandwidth caps) and/or testing against a real socket to expose those bugs
